intents.intent: Two additions that keep every session's auto-loaded context flat as the OS grows. (1) Auto-loaded files carry current truth only: in CLAUDE.md, 02-identity, 03-conventions and 01-hot, a superseded dated line relocates to 00-09-system/11-decision-log.md at sync time — never deleted, just moved out of the every-session payload; elsewhere history stays inline. (2) Context budgets, measured by memory-sync every run: CLAUDE.md 8,000 characters, 02-identity 5,500, 03-conventions 7,500, 01-hot body 2,500, each brief's '## Now' 1,200 — over budget is a finding, fixed by tightening prose or relocating history, never by dropping a live warning or deleting provenance. Also a 'Build pipeline' section for visible work: the routing test ('will a human ever see a screen this creates or changes?') sends UI work through dubleslash-fidelity-gate before building and dubleslash-design-review after — two review moments only, gate passed = contract; and before a multi-session build ships, one review over the whole change, then walk the real result as its user.
intents.apply: Extend the existing 'Append, don't silently rewrite' section with the relocation rule, and add 'Context budgets' and 'Build pipeline' as their own sections. Preserve the user's own wording where they have customized; add what is absent.
intents.verify: 03-conventions.md states the relocation rule with 11-decision-log as the destination, lists the five budgets, and contains the build-pipeline routing test with both review moments and the whole-change-review-then-walk rule.

intents.intent: A sixth habit: before something ships, review the whole of it — then walk it. When work grew across several sessions or steps, ask for one review of the whole change before it goes out, not just the last step — each step can be individually fine while the seams hide the real problem. Then walk the real thing yourself, as the person it's for: click the actual flow, open the actual file. 'Each part is correct' and 'it works' are different claims, and only the walk tests the second one.
intents.apply: Add as a new numbered habit section before the Links footer, in the note's existing voice.
intents.verify: 08-using-claude.md contains a habit about whole-change review before shipping and personally walking the real result.

intents.intent: Two rules that keep the Bottom Line block from becoming noise. (1) A DECIDE is stated in full exactly once — in the turn that raises it; while it stays open in later turns it collapses to ONE line under OPEN, restated in full only if new information changes the question or the recommendation. (2) Status-only turns get a minimal block — Done + NEXT only, never a re-print of standing decisions.
intents.apply: Add both as rules in the existing Bottom Line rules list. If the user deleted the Bottom Line section entirely (the section says they may), skip this intent and say so in the receipt.
intents.verify: The Bottom Line rules include the stated-once rule and the minimal status-only block, or the section is absent by the user's choice and the receipt says so.

intents.intent: The capture hook must not file machine text as the user's words. In Claude Code transcripts, harness-injected text (task notifications, command output, reminders) arrives on user-role lines exactly like the human's own messages; measured on real transcripts, the overwhelming majority of user-role lines matching the capture heuristic were injected, not typed. Three precise changes: (a) skip any transcript line whose parsed object is null or has isMeta true; (b) skip any user-role line whose content opens with a harness envelope tag — add a case-insensitive regex constant that matches when the content, after optional leading whitespace, begins with '<' or '</' followed immediately by one of these tag names: task-notification, command-name, command-message, command-args, local-command-stdout, local-command-caveat, system-reminder, scheduled-task, session-start-hook, or hook- followed by letters (a bare tag name without the angle bracket must NOT match — real user text may start with those words); drop user-role lines that match; (c) parsing the hook's stdin payload must tolerate a literal null — coerce a null parse result to an empty object so the hook exits 0 instead of crashing.
intents.apply: Apply as minimal, surgical edits to the existing code — add the constant and the three guards without restructuring anything else. After editing, confirm the file still parses (for example: node --check .claude/hooks/capture.mjs).
intents.verify: Feeding the hook a transcript where the only SIGNAL-matching user line sits inside a task-notification envelope appends nothing to the inbox; a genuine user line still captures; echoing the literal string null into the hook exits 0 with no stack trace.
